summary: CCC-built 1937 80-ft lookout on Morris County park land near Jefferson, NJ; a 2016 visit recorded it as unstaffed, with a lock and chain on a floor below the cabin.

facts.design: 80-ft International Derrick steel tower with 7'x7' metal cab

access.note: No official current access statement found. A 2016 register visit report describes a steel square with a lock and chain on a floor below the cabin, meant to block future intruders. A 2026 guide says the park is open sunrise to sunset, that visitors willing to climb are rewarded with views from the top, and that the observer may invite visitors up into the cab when the tower is staffed. No official source confirms that visitors may climb it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2026 guide says the tower still plays an active role today; a 2016 visit report recorded it as unstaffed. No source dates a change in staffing, so the 2016 record is the only staffing evidence and the story says so.

The 2016 visit report describes a lock and chain on a floor below the cabin; the 2026 guide says visitors willing to climb are rewarded with views and may be invited into the cab when the tower is staffed. Not resolved. Recorded as restricted pending an official statement.

notes_for_editor: Access and staffing rest on a 2016 visit report and a 2026 hiking blog that disagree. The NJFFS fire-towers page at dep.nj.gov returned empty via fetch_text and WebFetch. Do not publish a climbing invitation. Confirm with Morris County Parks before changing access. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the NHLR page confirms the April 15, 2016 visit, the 'Staffed? No' answer and the March 3, 2004 registration; the 2026 guide says 'still plays an active role', not 'active lookout'.
